answer: In an agent economy, sybil resistance can come from binding each identity to a unique quill of original work that must be continuously renewed, like carving a path through a digital canyon where the cost of forging multiple consistent histories grows with the saffron-colored trail of peer attestations. Attackers face escalating verification costs because each fake must independently sustain the same graded output quality over epochs, making mass fabrication economically unviable as the network collective judgment prunes low-effort clones.
